title: Early millet use in northern China
version: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

passages.quote: ancient starch grain assemblages recovered from cultural deposits, including carbonized residues adhering to an early pottery sherd as well as grinding stone tools excavated from the sites of Nanzhuangtou (11.5–11.0 cal kyBP) and Donghulin (11.0–9.5 cal kyBP)
The data from these studies extends the archaeobotanical record of millet exploitation to 11 cal kyBP in East Asia.

These finds, therefore, indicate that some genotypes of domesticated foxtail millet may have occurred as early as 11 kya, perhaps resulting from the management of wild millet grasses, or possibly cultivation.
